sentences.text:
Complainant
 versus
Sh. Afzal Ahmad
S/o Sh. Kalu Khan
M/s Afzal Kiryana Store,
B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park,
Delhi - 53 ... Accused
Judgment:

1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 14.02.2005, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh R.K.
Bhaskar and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Sh Naubat Singh under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as DA vs Afzal Ahmad LHA)/SDM Sh Sameer C.
Menz visited the premises of M/s Afzal Kiryana Store, B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park, Delhi - 53, where the accused Afzal Ahmad was found conducting the business of above mention shop,
having stored food articles including "Mustard Oil" for human consumption.

entities.text:
DA vs Afzal Ahmad LHA)/SDM Sh Sameer C.
Menz
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Food Inspector disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Mustard Oil" from the vendor for analysis.
The sample consisted of approx. 750 gms of Mustard Oil taken from an open tin container having no label declaration.

The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh.
Sameer C. Menz, SDM/LHA.
The sample of "Mustard Oil" was taken after proper mixing with the help of measure already lying in the tine container by rotating it in all possible directions.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles.

Each sample bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/
1 PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice in Form VI was given to accused Afzal Ahmad and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 14.02.2005.
Panchnama was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.l. were signed by accused Afzal Ahmad and the other witness FA Sh Naubat Singh.
Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such FA Sh.Naubat Singh was joined as witness.

3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No 52/LHA/10652 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact DA vs Afzal Ahmad condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be adulterated.

The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with non permitted synthetic oil soluble coal tar dye.

It also does not conform to standard with respect to BR,
Saponification Value & un-saponifiable matter exceed the prescribed maximum limit of 60.5, 177 and 1.2% respectively and BTT is not within limit.
The sample contains admixture of rice bran oil."

It is further stated that the vendor was selling "Mustard Oil" in unpacked condition which is banned in Delhi vide notification No. F5(25)/98/PFA/Enf./5034 dated 27.08.98 issued by the Food (Health) Authority in pursuance of provisions of Clause (iv) of Section 7 of PFA Act, 1954.

4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Afzal Ahmad was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Afzal Kiryana Store, B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park, Delhi - 53 at the time of sampling and he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.
5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.06.2005 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(b)(h)(j)(l)&(m) of PFA Act and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 & Rule 44 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.
DA vs Afzal Ahmad 6.
As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.06.2005.
The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act.
The CFL reported that the sample did not confirm to standards as it was detected with non permitted synthetic oil and and saponification value exceeded the maximum limits.

Based on the report of the CFL and pre charge evidence charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(b)(j)&(m) and Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

2 7.

At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI R.K.
Bhaskar, PW-2 FA Naubat Singh, PW-3 S.C. Menz, PW-4 SDM/LHA Sh R.K. Chauhan.
PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar, PW-2 FA Naubat Singh were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Sh S.C. Menz.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of Mustard Oil approx. 750 gms from an open tin container bearing no identical label declaration and dividing it into three parts by putting in three clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's DA vs Afzal Ahmad receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C.
The vendor furnished his statement Ex.PW1/C2 at the spot and the notification banning the sale of loose mustard oil Ex.PW1/C1.

Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample alongwith copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII was deposited on th enext working day i.e. 15.02.2005 in intact condition with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D and two remaining counterparts of the sample in intact condition alongwith two copies of Memos in Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex.PW-1/E.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW-1/F was received, according to which the sample found adulterated because it was coloured with unpermitted synthetic oil soluble colouring matter.

Thereafter PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar further investigated the matter and during investigation, he sent letter to STO, Ward No.75 and received its reply stating that no such firm was found registered with Sales Tax PW-1 FI
R.K. Bhaskar also sent letter Ex.PW1/H to DHO, Naveen Shahadra Zone and received reply stating that no health license was issued to the accused.

Thereafter, on completion of investigation, the entire case file was sent before the concerned SDM/LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Shri Diwan Chand granted his Consent for prosecution of accused persons after applying his mind vide Ex. PW1/I.

Thereafter on the instruction of PW-4 SDM/LHA Sh R.K.
Chauhan, the present complaint Ex.PW1/J was filed before the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/K alongwith copies of PA's Reports were sent to the accused persons through post vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/L.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel.
DA vs Afzal Ahmad 8.
Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 28.08.2015 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Thereafter the matter was fixed for defence evidence.
9. In defence evidence, the accused examined Sh S.N. Mehendru as DW-1.
Thereafter, vide order dated 30.04.2016, the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
10. In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
11.The present case alleges adulteration in the sample of mustard oil collected from the business concern of the accused.

This sample of mustard oil has been analysed twice, firstly by the PA and Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/
3 secondly, by the CFL.

entities.text: PA and Da vs Afzal Ahmad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. As per section 13(3) of the PFA Act, the certificate issued by the Director of CFL shall supersede the report of the PA.
As per proviso to section 13(5) of the Act, such certificate shall be final and conclusive evidence for the facts stated therein.
Thus, as far as the findings of the CFL are concerned, the same are final and conclusive and no evidence can be given to disprove the same.

13. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR DA vs Afzal Ahmad 1999 SC 738],
it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned.

entities.text: Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR DA vs Afzal Ahmad 1999 SC 738]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents.

entities.text: Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Director is a greater expert and therefore the statute says that his certificate shall be accepted by the court as conclusive evidence.
For all purposes the report of the public analyst is replaced by the certificate of the Director....
Superseded is a strong word.
It means obliterate, set aside, annul, replace, make void, inefficacious or useless, repeal.
The Director's certificate supersedes the report given by the public analyst.
Once superseded it does not survive for any purpose.
It will be anomalous to hold that for some purpose it survives and for other purposes it is superseded."
15. The scheme of Act would show that CFL has been, in a way, given the status of an appellate expert over the findings of PA.

In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed that "According to the scheme of the Act, the Director of Central Food Laboratory is constituted to be a sort of greater DA vs Afzal Ahmad expert than the Public Analyst and his certificate supersedes the report of Public Analyst under sub-section (3) of section 13".

The Hon'ble Court also took a note of the ruling in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970] wherein it was observed that the right has been given to the vendor for his satisfaction and proper defence, to get the sample analysed by a "greater expert whose certificate is to be accepted by court as conclusive evidence".

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. What is important to be noted is, that no such finality and conclusiveness has been attached to the report of PA and it has been only attached to the report of CFL.
Reliance can be placed on Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Zahiruddin [ILR (1972) 1 Del 630].

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Zahiruddin [ILR (1972) 1 Del 630]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, evidence can be given by the accused to disprove the report of PA, but once the accused exercises his right under section 13(2) of the Act upon which Certificate is given by CFL, such a certificate of CFL would supersede the PA report and would become final and conclusive.
17. The sample analysed in the present case is that of mustard oil.
The adulteration alleged as per CFL report is that this mustard oil was detected with non permitted synthetic oil soluble colour with higher saponification value.
Rule 29 PFA Rules prohibits the addition of synthetic colour in the Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/

4 sample commodity i.e. mustard oil and therefore the addition of synthetic colour amounts to violation of PFA Rules.
18.
Now come to the defence raised by the accused.
The first defence is that the sample purchased was not a representative DA vs Afzal Ahmad sample as there are variations in the report of PA and CFL.

In the CFL report, saponification value is shown as 180.42 whereas in PA it is 186.04.
19.
As far as this aspect is concerned, it has already been discussed that once the sample is analysed by CFL, its report supersedes the report of Public Analyst.
Since the report of PA is superseded by CFL, it cannot be used for the purpose of comparing with the CFL and to look for variations.
Otherwise also the adulteration alleged is that the mustard oil was coloured with synthetic colouring material.

Both the CFL and PA report says that synthetic colour was present in the mustard oil and therefore on this issue there is no variations between both the reports.
20.
The next ground of defence is that no public person has been joined in the sample collection proceedings violating section 10(7) of PFA Act.
The fate of the case depends on quality of witnesses and not their quantity or designation or professions.
There is no rule of law that requires the evidence of food officials to be viewed with any suspicion.
What is required is that attempt is made to join public persons as witnesses as a matter of prudence.
The court is not oblivious of reluctance of public persons to join such legal proceedings that involves lengthy procedural formalities and strict future commitments.
But non joining of such witnesses would not negate the testimony of official witnesses when they are otherwise truthful and credit worthy and have withstood the test of cross- examination.
No motive has shown to exist giving them reason to depose falsely against the accused persons.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC DA vs Afzal Ahmad (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed,
is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.

entities.text: Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC DA vs Afzal Ahmad (SC) 483]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No such inconsistency can be seen in this case.
No violation of any rule or provision has been pointed out by the defence.
All the witnesses in this case have supported and corroborated the version of each other.

All deposed about their presence at the spot, sampling proceedings, preparation of documents, etc.
21.

Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature,
substance or quality which it purported or represented to be.
Section 2(ia)(b) it has to be established that the food article contains any other substance which injuriously affect the nature, substance or quality thereof.
Section 2(ia)(j) specifically deals with colouring matter which is present other than prescribed or is present beyond the prescribed limits of variability.

Section 2(ia)(m) of PFA Act deals with situation where the quality or purity of an article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability.
Therefore on the basis of aforesaid discussion, it is clear that the mustard oil which was collected by the Food Inspector from the accused was adulterated with synthetic colour.

The violation of section 2(ia)(a),
(b), (j) and (m) of the PFA Act read with Rules 23 and 29 of PFA Rules stands DA vs Afzal Ahmad established in this case.

Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/
5 22.

On the basis of the aforesaid discussions, the accused Afzal Ahmad is convicted for offence u/s 16(1)(A) of PFA Act.
23.
List the matter for arguments on sentence.
